payload.reasoning_summary: FASE-1 is the earliest incomplete phase and the repository has no production workspace. Accept a reduced, reviewable foundation from IDEA-001: establish the mandated package topology and make strict compilation, determinism lint, and dependency-boundary lint blocking before production logic is introduced. Electron, installers, and feature implementation remain separate FASE-1 work.
risks: Some Section 13 restrictions require custom ESLint rules or AST-aware checks; superficial text matching could miss aliased or indirect violations.
A boundary checker that validates only package manifests but not source imports could permit architectural violations.
Creating every mandated directory now can encourage placeholder code; placeholders must remain configuration-only and must not encode future design decisions.

acceptance_criteria: All mandated directories exist and are registered in the workspace; workspace installation succeeds from the committed lockfile.
Every TypeScript project inherits strict:true and noUncheckedIndexedAccess:true, and the root compile command exits successfully.
The lint configuration treats all packages as pure by default and limits impurity exceptions to the packages explicitly permitted by the specification.

The blocking lint command rejects representative uses of Math.random, wall-clock APIs, prohibited transcendental Math functions, fetch, console, nondeterministic collection traversal, comparator-free Array.sort, forbidden JSON serialization of economic structures, and Node/Electron imports from pure packages.
The dependency-boundary command rejects imports outside the Section 14.5 directed graph and exits successfully for the repository's valid imports.
CI runs clean installation, compilation, lint, dependency-boundary validation, and tests; every job passes on the committed repository state.
SPEC_BLOCKERS.md exists and provides the Section 19 fields without inventing or resolving a specification contradiction.
No production algorithm or unresolved DEFINIR-dependent behavior is introduced.
must_preserve: The frozen specification and benchmark files remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
Existing benchmark history, checkpoint, and orchestration scaffolding remain untouched.
Pure packages cannot import Node or Electron APIs.
No DEFINIR decision is embedded in implementation before its required ADR.
All gates are blocking and cannot pass by silently excluding newly added package source files.
task.objective: Create the FASE-1 workspace foundation with strict TypeScript and executable CI gates that reject prohibited nondeterminism and illegal package dependencies.
out_of_scope: Electron runtime implementation and BrowserWindow security configuration.
Windows NSIS or Linux AppImage packaging.
ADRs for hash, rounding enforcement, canonical encoding, price mathematics, or octave parameters.
Production simulation, numeric, RNG, hashing, world, domain, application, replay, benchmark, or UI behavior.
Dependencies or architecture intended only for phases after FASE-1.
required_tests: Automated rule tests containing one failing fixture for each Section 13 prohibition category and passing fixtures for authorized code.
Automated boundary tests with at least one allowed edge and representative forbidden edges, including a transitive dependency violation.
A configuration test that enumerates workspace TypeScript projects and verifies strict and noUncheckedIndexedAccess remain enabled.
Run the same root compile, lint, boundary-check, and test commands locally and in CI.
scope: Create the root pnpm workspace and package manifests for packages/core, packages/world, packages/domain, packages/application, packages/narrative, packages/contracts, packages/adapters, packages/ui, apps/desktop/main, apps/desktop/preload, apps/desktop/renderer, apps/desktop/simulation-worker, tools/replay, tools/bench, tools/package, and docs/decisions.
Configure TypeScript 5.x with strict mode and noUncheckedIndexedAccess enabled for every workspace project.
Configure ESLint so packages are pure by default, with only the specification-authorized impure package exceptions, and make the Section 13 deterministic-code prohibitions blocking.
Implement a blocking dependency-boundary check for the directed package graph in Section 14.5.
Add root compile, lint, boundary-check, and test commands and run them in CI on pushes and pull requests.
Create SPEC_BLOCKERS.md using the Section 19 ambiguity-reporting structure.
Add minimal fixtures/tests proving the lint and dependency gates reject representative forbidden cases rather than merely configuring rules.
